keyDecisions.decision: Load Turf.js in fixture.ts via `page.addScriptTag({ path: resolveTurfBrowserBundle() })` instead of the old CDN URL, resolving the bundle's path through @turf/turf's package.json export rather than its unexported turf.min.js deep path.
keyDecisions.reasoning: @turf/turf@6's package.json `exports` map only allows '.' and './package.json' — `require.resolve('@turf/turf/turf.min.js')` throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Resolving via './package.json' and joining its directory with the known sibling filename (listed in that same package.json's `files`/`browser` fields) stays within the exports contract and makes the suite work fully offline.

keyDecisions.decision: Fixed checkTileFailures()'s detection logic from a '.leaflet-tile-loaded.leaflet-tile-error' DOM-class check to an img.complete && naturalWidth===0 check.
keyDecisions.reasoning: Verified by reading node_modules/leaflet/dist/leaflet-src.js's _tileReady: this installed Leaflet version (1.9.x) never adds a 'leaflet-tile-error' class on tile failure — the old check could never return true. Discovered while proving each helper's test can fail (AC3): deliberately pointing the fixture's tile URL at a 404 path left checkTileFailures() returning false regardless. This is a pre-existing defect in the helper itself, not a test authoring issue, and AC3 cannot be satisfied for this helper without fixing it. The public signature and documented behavior ('Returns true if any map tiles failed to load') are unchanged.

keyDecisions.decision: Built fixtures/assets/tile.png as a hand-generated, zlib-deflated 16x16 RGB PNG rather than a copied/base64 placeholder image.
keyDecisions.reasoning: An initial hand-written base64 1x1 PNG passed Unix `file` magic-byte sniffing but Chrome reported naturalWidth/naturalHeight 0 for it — an undecoded, effectively broken image that would have made checkTileFailures()'s happy-path test accidentally pass for the wrong reason (same defect this order exists to avoid). Verified the replacement decodes correctly in real Chrome (naturalWidth: 16) before relying on it in any test.

keyDecisions.decision: tests/fixture.spec.ts imports `{ test }` from '../src/fixture' (TS source) rather than the package's own published name/dist output.
keyDecisions.reasoning: Matches the existing precedent in packages/saturday-playwright-k6-exporter/tests/fixture.spec.ts (imports from '../src/index'). Avoids a self-referential workspace:* dependency on the package's own package name, while AC4's docker command still builds the package first as part of its own precondition, independent of what the test imports.

keyDecisions.decision: fixtures/serve.mjs restricts its static routes to an explicit allow-list ({ '/leaflet/': ..., '/assets/': ... } plus exact matches for '/' and '/turf.min.js') with a resolveWithinRoot boundary check, rather than general directory listing.
keyDecisions.reasoning: No production code reads this file, but architecture-guardrails.md's conventions apply project-wide; an allow-list with a resolved-path boundary check is simpler to reason about and avoids any path-traversal surface even though this server only ever runs locally against trusted local requests.

deviations.task: architecture-notes.md's Developer Handoff Notes: 'Touch only the Turf.js script-tag line and its immediate surrounding code in src/fixture.ts for this order.'
deviations.reason: AC3 requires every helper's test to demonstrably fail when its fixture value changes. checkTileFailures()'s original DOM-class check could never fail (or pass) correctly against the installed Leaflet version — it was dead logic, not a scope boundary. Fixed its detection mechanism (see keyDecisions) without changing its name, signature, or documented return contract. Flagging explicitly since it's a second touch-point in fixture.ts beyond the Turf CDN line the handoff note anticipated.

dependenciesAdded.reason: Replaces the CDN-loaded turf.min.js (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@turf/turf@6/turf.min.js) so the suite works under AC4's --network none; same major version previously CDN-pinned. Lands in `dependencies` (not devDependencies) since fixture.ts loads its browser bundle into the page under test at runtime, the same category leaflet is already in.

fixture.ts's new resolveTurfBrowserBundle() uses node:path and require.resolve, which need Node's ambient types to compile under this package's existing strict tsconfig. Not previously needed since fixture.ts had no Node-API usage. Version pin matches apps/ye-olde-magic-shop's own @types/node pin for consistency.

That app's test suite was not re-run as part of this order (different bounded context, per architecture-notes.md); worth a check since the fix is more correct but means that test will now actually exercise its assertion where it silently couldn't before.

Cyclomatic complexity and the 'changed lines covered by a test that can fail' bar (per AC5) weren't run through analyze-complexity/eslint tooling — no such tool is configured for this package; self-reviewed by inspection only (see selfReview).
